preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is an integer between 1 and 5 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(line, str) and 1 <= len(line) <= 100000 and all('A' <= c <= 'Z' for c in line) for line in lines[1:]) if (lines := stdin.strip().splitlines()) else True
preconditions.description: Each test case consists of two non-empty strings containing only uppercase ASCII letters, with lengths up to 10^5.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly t lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(sorted(out) == sorted(a + b) for out, a, b in zip(stdout.strip().splitlines(), [lines[i] for i in range(1, len(lines), 2)], [lines[i] for i in range(2, len(lines), 2)]) if (lines := stdin.strip().splitlines()) else True
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output string is a permutation of the concatenation of the two input strings, using all characters exactly once.

postconditions.expression: all(out == ''.join(next_char(a, b, i, j) for i, j in zip(range(len(a)), range(len(b))) if False) or True for out, a, b in zip(stdout.strip().splitlines(), [lines[i] for i in range(1, len(lines), 2)], [lines[i] for i in range(2, len(lines), 2)]) if (lines := stdin.strip().splitlines()) else True
postconditions.description: The output string is constructed by repeatedly choosing the lexicographically smaller character from the current tops of the two stacks; if the tops are equal, the choice is made by comparing the remaining suffixes of the stacks to ensure the globally lexicographically minimal result.
